title: variance annotations on type parameters (TS 4.7)
witness:
export interface I<in T> { f(x: T): void }
export type F<out T> = () => T;

title: export type * re-exports (TS 5.0)
witness: export type * as Ns from "./m";

title: a class member named accessor
witness: export class C { accessor() { return 1; } }

title: typeof import() as a call's first type argument
witness:
declare function f<T>(): T;
export const a = f<typeof import('./m')>();

title: members of an import() type, with type arguments
witness:
export type A = keyof import('./m').A;
export type B = import('./m').B<string>;

title: type arguments on a tagged template
witness:
declare function f<T>(s: TemplateStringsArray): T;
export const a = f<string>`x`;

title: call signatures separated only by line breaks
no ASI before a member whose name starts with in
a generic function type with a default, split over lines
type as an exported name
witness:
const type = 1;
export { type };

title: a reserved word as a property after ?.
a using declaration reads as an assignment
witness:
declare function f(): Disposable;
export function g() { using x = f(); }
note: tree-sitter-javascript 0.23.1 takes `using` as an anonymous prefix of assignment_expression; 0.25.0 adds the declaration

title: of as a binding name in for-of reads let as the binding
witness:
for (let of of [1]) {}
export {};
note: `for (let of of [1])` reads as `let` iterating `of[1]`; fixed in tree-sitter-javascript 0.25.0

title: an invalid escape in a tagged template
witness: export const p = String.raw`C:\Users`;

title: export default of a declaration
witness: export default let a = 42;

title: a reserved word as a binding name
witness:
var enum = 1;
export {};

title: await and yield regardless of context
witness: export function f() { yield 1; }

title: a method's decorators sit outside method_definition
witness:
declare const d: any;
export class A { @d m() {} }

title: an exported class's decorator attaches to the export
witness:
declare const d: any;
@d export class A {}

title: the non-null assertion's precedence
await of a call with type arguments
witness:
declare function f<T>(): Promise<T>;
export async function g() { await f<string>(); }

title: an anonymous default-exported function is an expression
witness: export default function () {}

title: a labelled statement
a destructuring assignment
ASI after an arrow function followed by a parenthesized expression
&raw[..] when the identifier is named raw
note: fixed by v0.24.1, a git tag only: npm still publishes 0.24.0 (rust#318)

title: string literals with unexpected prefixes, and recovery after repeated string literals
a block comment with multibyte characters
<= after a cast
two attributes on a parameter
witness: pub fn f(#[allow(unused)] #[allow(unused)] x: u8) {}

title: safe items in an unsafe extern block (edition 2024)
a trailing comma in closure parameters
a where clause on a unit struct
attributes on struct pattern fields
a tilde in a macro token tree
witness:
macro_rules! m { ($($t:tt)*) => {} }
m!(~);

title: * after .. is a binary operator
suffixes on integer literals
attributes and doc comments attach to the wrong item
rustc's own test files that tree-sitter rejects (a list of about 50)
a generic class (PEP 695, 3.12)
type parameter defaults (PEP 696, 3.13)
witness:
def f[T = int](x: T) -> T:
    return x

title: an assignment through type(...) reads as a type alias
witness: type(_).foo = bar

title: | in an annotation reads as a binary operator
witness: def f(arg: bytes | int | float): pass

title: a list splat in a call
witness: x = [*map(slice, a, b)]

title: a comment inside an if body

unpacking in comprehensions (PEP 798, 3.15)
witness:

ys = [*("p", x) for x in xs]

title: the lazy soft keyword (3.15)
